newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes lower, set in near-term range.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes lower, set in near-term range.

text.p: Gold prices looked to be settling into a range on Thursday after silver was sold off by the investment funds in New York late on Wednesday, dealers said.

"It's been a bit disappointing. You would have thought silver would be decoupling from the gold market but it has not," one dealer said referring to the prevailing bearish sentiment which has spread from gold to the other precious metals.
Gold fixed at $318.75 per ounce, just down from the $319.50 struck at both the morning and afternoon fixes on Wednesday.
"It seems to be in a range from $318.00-$322.00 with physical interest picking up at under $320.00," a dealer said.
The $322-$323 area which the price touched briefly on July 14 and July 8, would invite plenty of selling, he added.

Gold prices have been under pressure all year and the pressure increased at the beginning of this month when the Australian central bank announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves over the previous six months.
The sum amounted to two-thirds of Australia's gold reserves. The country is the third largest miner of gold after South Africa and the United States.
The news dropped the gold price to 12-year lows and brought several mines to the point were they cannnot cover costs.
The first casualty was Botoni Mining in South Africa which is to cease production and go on care and maintainence.
Gold has failed to re-attract investors in the face of competition from potentially more attractive profits on booming stock markets and a safer store of capital in a thriving U.S. dollar.
The low price has led Australian producers to postpone expansion plans.
Most dramatically WMC Ltd put on hold a A$157 million expansion of its St Ives mine in Western Australia that would have eventually lifted output to around 700,000 ounces a year from 400,000 ounces.
General Gold NL is shutting down its Mount Monger mine and North Ltd has cast doubt over the near-term development of its Lake Cowal mine.
Silver was indicated at $4.21/$4.23 down eight cents. "Expect to see the funds have another go at it targeting $4.00," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were lightly sold at $403.00/$406.00 down $2.00 and $173.00/$175.00 down $1.75 respectively.
This was despite a report that Russia would not ship its first platinum of the year to Japan until next week.
